summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with dysuria, fever, chills, and right flank pain following recent completion of Bactrim for a prior UTI. She has a complex medical history including recurrent UTIs with chronic cystitis, HIV, hepatitis B and C, morbid obesity, and chronic pain. Urinalysis showed pyuria and bacteriuria, and preliminary urine culture grew >100,000 colonies of E. coli. Given her history of resistant infections, she was treated with IV imipenem after initial ceftriaxone in the ED. Symptoms resolved during the two-day admission, and she completed eight doses of antibiotics. Chronic issues including HIV, anticoagulation with warfarin, and pain management were maintained on home regimens. She was discharged home with instructions to continue all medications, take phenazopyridine for three days, monitor weight, and follow up with her primary care provider for final culture results and INR monitoring.
